label: Root links from Bertrand Russell, The Philosophy of Logical Atomism
summary: V.66–68: Russell explains general existence by some value satisfying a propositional function. Using this account against the case's proposed object-level existence feature requires treating that feature as exhausted by the same quantificational reading. It does not deny that the function is exemplified. V.71–72: Russell acknowledges existential and general facts without a complete analysis of them by the formula. His limitation prevents treating the propositional-function paraphrase alone as an exhaustive account of a case existence fact. A further connection between those facts and the case's reality feature is open. V.75–76: Russell treats universe nonemptiness and the number of things as empirical questions. Reading the case's two-bearer assertion this way requires matching its selected-world candidate domain to that empirical inventory. Formal possibility of two inhabitants does not supply the actual observations. V.77: Russell denies meaningful predication of the same existence notion of an actually named object. Comparison requires identifying the case's reality feature with Russell's quantifier reading and the bearer with a genuinely named object, rather than treating his claim as a denial of every object-level notion of esse. VI.78–81: Russell takes a genuine name to have a referent, and treats a significant denial of existence such as the Romulus example through a description. Applying the doctrine to the naming route needs to establish whether the target term is a proper name in this strict sense or a name introduced by a nominal description. VI.86–87: Russell's test for the existence of a singular described individual requires both a satisfier and uniqueness. If the route really uses such a description, the application needs both conditions for the same descriptor. Naming from a satisfied profile alone does not implement that semantic analysis. VI.90–91: Russell withholds a transfer from existential satisfaction of a description to predicating existence of a genuinely named individual. The naming route needs an explicit transition from its nominal description to the same proper referent before drawing that stronger predicative conclusion.
